children: CHARLOTTE, N.C., Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JELD-WEN Holding, Inc. (
) ("JELD-WEN" or the "Company") today announced results for the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026. Comparability is to the same period in the prior year.

Net revenues of $798.5 million decreased (1.4%) in the third quarter driven by a decrease in Core Revenues of (1%). The decline in Core Revenues was driven by a (2%) decrease in volume/mix, partially offset by a 1% benefit from price realization.

Net loss was ($17.2) million or ($0.20) per share, compared to net loss of ($367.6) million, or ($4.30) per share, during the same quarter a year ago. Operating income (loss) margin was 1.1% and (25.0%) for the quarters ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, respectively.

Adjusted EBITDA was $54.4 million, an increase of $10.0 million compared to $44.4 million during the same quarter a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA Margin was 6.8%, an increase of 130 basis points in the third quarter primarily due to  tariff refunds recognized as a reduction in cost of sales, favorable productivity, and lower SG&A expense, partially offset by negative price/cost and volume/mix.
Commenced transactions to extend debt maturities and raise $135.0 million of incremental liquidity.
Concluded the strategic review of the European business; retaining the business, with a focus on operational improvements and cost reductions, provides the best opportunity to create long-term value.

"Our third-quarter results reflect the continued progress we are making to strengthen our business, even as market conditions remain challenging," said Chief Executive Officer William J. Christensen. "We remain focused on improving service, managing costs, and driving productivity, which are helping us improve our competitive position. Despite a softer market outlook, we are maintaining our full-year revenue and Adjusted EBITDA guidance while making important progress on our strategic priorities, including our debt refinancing and the future of our European business."

Net revenues decreased ($11.0) million, or (1.4%), to $798.5 million in the three months ended September 26, 2026, from $809.5 million in the three months ended September 27, 2025. The decrease in net revenues was primarily driven by a decrease  in Core Revenues of (1%). The decline in Core Revenues was driven by a (2%) decrease in volume/mix, partially offset by a 1% benefit from price realization.

Net loss was ($17.2) million in the third quarter, compared to a net loss of ($367.6) million in the same period last year. Adjusted Net Income for the third quarter was $4.4 million, an increase of $21.6 million compared to Adjusted Net Loss of ($17.3) million in the same period last year.

Net loss per share for the third quarter was ($0.20), compared to a net loss per share of ($4.30) in the same quarter last year. Adjusted EPS for the third quarter was $0.05, compared to ($0.20) in the same quarter last year. Adjusted EPS for the quarter ended September 26, 2026, excludes net after-tax charges of $21.6 million, or $0.25 per diluted share. Adjusted EPS for the quarter ended September 27, 2025, excludes net after-tax charges of $350.3 million or $4.10 per diluted share. Third quarter 2025 net loss from continuing ops includes $196.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment and $122.3 million tax special items.

Adjusted EBITDA was $54.4 million, an increase of $10.0 million compared to $44.4 million during the same quarter last year. Adjusted EBITDA Margin was 6.8%, an increase of 130 basis points in the third quarter primarily due to tariff refunds recognized as a reduction in cost of sales, favorable productivity, and lower SG&A expense, partially offset by negative price/cost and volume/mix.
On a segment basis for the third quarter of 2026, compared to the same period last year:

- Net revenues decreased ($16.5) million, or (3.0%), to $529.7 million in the three months ended September 26, 2026, from $546.1 million in the three months ended September 27, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a decrease in Core Revenues of (3%). The decrease in Core Revenues was driven by a (3%) decline in volume/mix due to weakened market demand. Net income was $21.2 million, an increase of $202.4 million year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA in North America increased $10.7 million, or 28.3%, to $48.3 million in the three months ended September 26, 2026, from $37.7 million in the three months ended September 27, 2025. The increase was primarily due to tariff refunds recognized as a reduction in cost of sales, improved productivity, and lower SG&A, partially offset by unfavorable price/cost and volume/mix.

- Net revenues increased $5.5 million, or 2.1%, to $268.9 million in the three months ended September 26, 2026, from $263.3 million in the three months ended September 27, 2025. The increase was primarily due to an increase in Core Revenues of 3%, partially offset by an unfavorable foreign exchange impact of (1%). The increase in Core Revenues was primarily driven by a 4% benefit from price realization, partially offset by unfavorable volume/mix of (1%). Net loss was ($6.9) million, an increase of $146.5 million year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA in Europe decreased ($1.0) million, or (6.5%), to $15.0 million in the three months ended September 26, 2026, from $16.0 million in the three months ended September 27, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to unfavorable price/cost and higher bad debt expense, partially offset by lower salaries and benefits and improved productivity.

Net cash used in operating activities was ($72.8) million in the nine months ended September 26, 2026, compared to ($37.7) million in the nine months ended September 27, 2025, an increase in cash used of $35.1 million. The change in cash flows from operating activities was primarily attributable to lower earnings, excluding the prior year impact of the $334.6 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge related to our North America and Europe reporting units and the $129.2 million income tax expense due to an increase to valuation allowances on U.S. tax attributes. Changes in our working capital accounts resulted in a $59.6 million unfavorable year-over-year impact. Accounts receivable, net resulted in a ($36.9) million unfavorable impact, primarily due to the timing of revenue recognition and customer collections. Accounts payable resulted in a ($15.1) million unfavorable impact, primarily due to lower inventory purchases and timing of vendor payments. Inventory resulted in a ($7.6) million unfavorable impact, primarily reflecting a decrease in inventory reserves.

Capital expenditures in the nine months ended September 26, 2026, decreased by $46.7 million to $57.2 million, down from $103.9 million in the nine months ended September 27, 2025. Free Cash Flow used in the nine months ended September 26, 2026, was ($129.9) million, compared to Free Cash Flow used in the nine months ended September 27, 2025, of ($141.6) million. This does not include the impact of proceeds of $110.7 million from the court-ordered divestiture of our Towanda facility, which was completed in the first quarter of 2025.

JELD-WEN is maintaining its 2026 revenue guidance of $3.1 to $3.2 billion. This range reflects a year-over-year decline in Core Revenues of approximately (2%) to (5%), compared to 2025, and a foreign exchange benefit of approximately $50 million. Additionally, the Company continues to expect Adjusted EBITDA to be in the range of $120 to $150 million, reflecting significant cost reductions, partially offset by continued price/cost and volume pressure.
The Company expects 2026 operating cash flow to generate approximately $10 million.

This press release presents certain "non-GAAP" financial measures, including Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations, Adjusted EBITDA Margin from continuing operations, Adjusted Net Income (Loss) from continuing operations, Adjusted EPS from continuing operations, Free Cash Flow, and Net Debt Leverage. The components of these non-GAAP measures are computed by using amounts that are determined in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("GAAP"). A reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures used in this press release to their nearest comparable GAAP financial measures is included in the tables at the end of this press release.

The Company provides certain guidance solely on a non-GAAP basis because the Company cannot predict certain elements that are included in certain reported GAAP results. While management cannot provide a reconciliation of items for forward-looking non-GAAP measures without unreasonable effort, management bases the estimated ranges of non-GAAP measures for future periods on its reasonable estimates of certain items such as assumed effective tax rate, assumed interest expense, and other assumptions about capital requirements for future periods. Although the Company believes the assumptions reflected in the range of its 2026 guidance are reasonable, actual results could vary substantially given the uncertainty regarding the future performance of the global economy, ongoing geopolitical conflicts, disruptions in supply chains, and changes in raw material prices and other costs as well as other risks and uncertainties, including those described below. In addition, the guidance ranges provided for 2026 do not include the impact of potential acquisitions or divestitures. The variability of these items may have a significant impact on our future GAAP results.

Other companies may compute these measures differently. The non-GAAP information has limitations as an analytical tool and should not be considered in isolation from or as a substitute for U.S. GAAP information. It does not purport to represent any similarly titled U.S. GAAP information and is not an indicator of our performance under U.S. GAAP.

We present several financial metrics in "Core" terms, which exclude the impact of foreign exchange, acquisitions and divestitures completed in the last twelve months. We define Core Revenues as net revenues excluding the impact of foreign exchange, and acquisitions and divestitures completed in the last twelve months. The use of "Core" metrics assists management, investors, and analysts in understanding the organic performance of the operations.

We use Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations, Adjusted EBITDA Margin from continuing operations, Adjusted Net Income (Loss) from continuing operations, and Adjusted EPS from continuing operations because we believe they assist investors and analysts in comparing our operating performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that we do not believe are indicative of our core operating performance. Management believes Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations and Adjusted EBITDA Margin from continuing operations are helpful in highlighting trends because they exclude certain items outside the control of management, while other measures can differ significantly depending on long-term strategic decisions regarding capital structure, the tax jurisdictions in which we operate, and capital investments. We use Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations and Adjusted EBITDA Margin from continuing operations to measure our financial performance in reporting our results to our Board of Directors. Further, our executive incentive compensation is based in part on Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations should not be considered as an alternative to net income as a measure of financial performance or to cash flows from operations as a liquidity measure.

We define Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations as income (loss) from continuing operations, net of tax, adjusted for the following items: income tax expense (benefit); depreciation and amortization; interest expense (income), net; and certain special items consisting of non-recurring net legal and professional expenses and settlements; goodwill impairment; restructuring and asset-related charges, net; M&A related costs, net; net (gain) loss on sale of business, property and equipment; loss on extinguishment and refinancing of debt; share-based compensation expense; and other special items. We use Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations because we believe this measure assists investors and analysts in comparing our operating performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that we do not believe are indicative of our core operating performance.

Adjusted Net Income (Loss) from continuing operations represents loss from continuing operations adjusted for the after-tax impact of certain special items used to calculate Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations as described above. Where applicable, the specifically identified items are tax effected at the applicable jurisdictional tax rate and tax expense is adjusted to remove the effect of discrete tax items.

Adjusted EPS from continuing operations represents loss from continuing operations per diluted share adjusted to exclude the estimated per share impact of the same specifically identified items used to calculate Adjusted Net Income (Loss) from continuing operations as described above.
Adjusted EBITDA Margin from continuing operations represents Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations as a percentage of net revenues.

We present Free Cash Flow because we believe this metric assists investors and analysts in determining the quality of our earnings. Free Cash Flow is defined as net cash used in operating activities less capital expenditures (including purchases of intangible assets). Free Cash Flow should not be considered as an alternative to net cash used in operating activities as a liquidity measure. We also present Net Debt Leverage because it is a key financial metric that is used by management to assess the balance sheet risk of the Company. We define Net Debt Leverage as Net Debt (total principal debt outstanding less unrestricted cash) divided by Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations for the last twelve-month period.

Net legal and professional expenses and settlements include non-recurring transformation journey expenses of $1.7 million and $5.8 million in the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026, respectively, and $5.3 million and $24.6 million in the three and nine months ended September 27, 2025, respectively. The amount for the nine months ended September 26, 2026, includes $1.2 million related to a structural-pricing initiative in Europe. These expenses primarily relate to discrete project-based consulting fees that directly support the Company's transformation journey and are not expected to represent normal, recurring operating expenses. These projects include the centralization of human resources processes, North America supply chain network optimization strategy, and other projects related to our transformation journey. These expenses also include $2.5 million for the nine months ended September 27, 2025, related to the engagement of a transformation consultant for a period spanning from the third quarter of 2023 through April 2025. Additionally, net legal and professional expenses and settlements include $0.4 million and $10.0 million in the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026, respectively, and $0.4 million in both the three and nine months ended September 27, 2025, relating to litigation of historical legal matters.
Goodwill impairment consists of a prior year goodwill impairment charge associated with our North America and Europe reporting units.

Restructuring and asset-related charges, net represents severance, accelerated depreciation and amortization, equipment relocation and other expenses directly incurred as a result of restructuring events. The restructuring charges primarily relate to charges incurred to change the operating structure, eliminate certain roles, and close certain manufacturing facilities in our North America and Europe segments.

Product and inventory-related charges represent charges associated with announced facility closures, including product-related cash charges recorded as a reduction of net revenues and inventory and other product-related non-cash charges recorded in cost of sales. These amounts are excluded from Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations.
M&A related costs, net consist of legal and professional expenses related to strategic initiatives and the court-ordered divestiture of Towanda.

Net gain on sale of business, property, and equipment in the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026, primarily relates to the sale of our business in Hawaii and the sale of property in Denmark. Net gain on sale of business, property, and equipment in the nine months ended September 27, 2025, primarily relates to the court-ordered divestiture of Towanda and the sale of property and equipment in Marion, North Carolina.
Loss on extinguishment and refinancing of debt consists of $0.2 million in the nine months ended September 27, 2025, associated with an amendment of our ABL Facility.
Share-based compensation expense represents equity-based compensation expense related to the issuance of share-based awards.

Other special items not core to ongoing business activity include: (i) for the three months ended September 26, 2026, impairment charges of $2.5 million recognized in connection with the Company's North America equipment capacity optimization review and a $1.0 million charge in Corporate and unallocated costs related to the termination of the Company's fractional aircraft arrangement.; (ii) for the nine months ended September 26, 2026, impairment charges of $5.6 million recognized in connection with the Company's North America equipment capacity optimization review, $3.0 million of impairment and other related charges related to windows manufacturing technology, and $1.8 million of impairment charges related to logistics technology, each of which was determined to have no future use, $2.5 million related to post-production expenses for closed facilities in North America, $1.2 million related to costs incurred to fulfill production capability requirements associated with the court-ordered Towanda divestiture, $2.0 million related to build-out costs for a new production site in the United Kingdom in our Europe reporting segment, and a $1.0 million charge in Corporate and unallocated costs related to the termination of the Company's fractional aircraft arrangement.
